title: ‘You will not be alone’: General Assembly President tells Rohingya refugees after genocide ruling
content: A day after the UN’s highest court found that Myanmar had committed genocide against the Rohingya, the President of the General Assembly visited the refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh, urging the world to turn the landmark judgement into action.

title: Haiti: ‘Atrocious abuses’ continue as UN warns anti-gang operations must priortise civilian protection
content: The UN human rights office, OHCHR has urged greater protection for civilians in Haiti amid ongoing “atrocious abuses” committed by gangs and intensified security operations.

title: ‘Peace begins in our hearts’: Children close Muscat forum with a message to the world
content: Children from across the world sent a message of peace from the Omani capital Muscat on Monday, calling for an end to hatred, respect for diversity and the protection of human rights.

title: Haiti: More than 1,000 killed between July and September, UN report reveals
content: More than 1,000 people were killed in Haiti during the third quarter of this year, as armed gangs continue to terrorize the population in the capital Port-au-Prince and beyond, the UN team in the island nation, said in its latest human rights report.

title: Egypt: Fact-checking site’s entire newsroom jailed as assault on press freedom widens
content: Six journalists who make up the entire newsroom of the Egyptian fact-checking website Matsadash remain in detention, the UN human rights office (OHCHR) said on Tuesday, warning of proliferating assaults on press freedom by the Government.

title: Sudan war: First ‘suicide’ drone attacks, now long-range strikes are the norm
content: Drones and drought are “closing in” on Sudan, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF), said on Tuesday, describing unprecedented attacks on the country’s infrastructure including by drones travelling up to 1,500 kilometres before hitting their target.

title: Afghanistan faces deepening humanitarian crisis amid sweeping rights restrictions
content: Afghanistan stands at a “difficult crossroad” more than five years after the Taliban returned to power, a senior UN official said on Friday. Relative stability and security are being undercut by a fragile economy, sweeping curbs on rights and acute humanitarian need.

title: DPR Korea: Isolation deepens even as the country changes, says UN rights official
content: The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) is building factories and hospitals, rolling out smartphones and mobile banking, and passing new laws at an unprecedented rate. But its people are more cut off from the outside world than at any point in the country’s history.

title: World News in Brief: 300,000 displaced in Lebanon, Türk ‘deeply concerned’ over Novaya Gazeta closure, $50 million refugee appeal, World Cities Day
content: More than 300,000 people displaced since early March remain internally displaced in Lebanon, where the humanitarian crisis is “far from over,” according to the UN’s aid coordination office (OCHA).

title: Myanmar’s illicit economy fuels escalating violence, with civilians bearing the brunt

title: World News in Brief: Russian attacks intensify, UN team tours West Bank, ‘unlawful’ elderly deaths

title: Bangladesh: UNICEF chief calls for an end to child marriage
content: At 14, Bushra faced being married off – until community leaders at a UNICEF-supported child protection hub worked with her father to prevent her from being given away against her will.

title: Hunger is ‘an avoidable tragedy’ in a world of plenty: Türk
content: More than a quarter of humanity struggles to get enough food, even though the world produces enough for everyone, UN human rights chief Volker Türk said on Monday, blaming injustice and the denial of human rights for hunger in a world of plenty.
